title: does recruit need mmseqs at all: count whether the mmseqs-only pairs concentrate in families that would lose their null
body: Answer it on MGnify over the 1000 shards, not on Swissprot: a bucket measured against 570k curated proteins says little about 2.4 billion metagenomic fragments. The four cutoffs-sp-* sets still hold their recruit tables and can be counted in minutes as a check.

notes.author: jackroddy/01dd6c44
notes.text: Counted over the 100 MGnify shards on disk, 245 million reversed sequences: nail recruited 10,579,765 (family, sequence) pairs, 94.75% of the union; mmseqs 957,796, 8.58%; both 371,975; mmseqs only 585,821, 5.25%; nail only 10,207,790. Per shard nail takes 140 s and mmseqs 177 s, steady across all 100. So mmseqs is 56% of the stage for 5.25% of the pairs, about 21x nail's cost per recruit nail would not have found. Dropping it takes the stage from 323 s to 141 s a shard, and the 1000 shards from 90 hours to 39. Both run at -s 11.0, --max-seqs 5000, E-value 10, and -k 6 for mmseqs. Not yet counted: whether the 585,821 are spread thinly or concentrated.

notes.author: jackroddy/21204bf1
notes.text: Ranked the 585,821 mmseqs-only pairs within each family's pooled mmseqs list over the 100 shards (script in tmp-claude/2026-10-06-mmseqs-only-rank/). They are 61% of mmseqs' own recruits and spread through the ranking rather than at the bottom: 18,670 of 19,615 families have one, 10,228 families have one at rank 1, 16,594 in the top 5, 2,895 families recruit only through mmseqs. Rank by E and by bits agree exactly. In absolute terms mmseqs' lists are weak: 92% of mmseqs-only pairs have E in (1,10], only 94 families have an mmseqs-only hit at E <= 1e-3; bits p50 31 for only and shared alike. Whether a weak mmseqs recruit becomes a high nail score at s12 with the prefilter off is unmeasured and is what decides it.

notes.author: jackroddy/21204bf1
notes.text: Shard 1, nail at 48 threads with no --mmseqs-max-seqs (nail's default is 2^31-1), otherwise recruit's flags; tables under tmp-claude/2026-10-06-nail-no-maxseqs/. Capped s11 from the run: 139 s, 106,327 pairs, 3,666 shared with mmseqs' 9,377. Uncapped s11: 197 s, 111,564 pairs, a strict superset of the capped run, 3,675 shared. Uncapped s12: 329 s, 123,501 pairs, 3,731 shared, but 6,913 of s11's pairs missing. mmseqs-only stays 5,702 and 5,646 of 9,377: the cap is not why nail misses them.

notes.author: jackroddy/21204bf1
notes.text: Side experiment (tmp-claude/2026-10-06-mmseqs-only-judge/): top 10 mmseqs-only recruits per family by E over the 100 shards, 143,145 pairs, 142,819 originals pulled from the reversed shards; all of Pfam against them with hmmsearch at -Z 2455940, 24 parts at --cpu 2, 222 s wall. Joined to the recruiting family, 568 pairs (0.4%) are rejects at E<=1e-3, flat across ranks 1-10; only 748 are hit at E<=10 at all. 18,526 of 18,670 families keep all of their top-5 mmseqs-only recruits as decoys. So they are decoys, not reversed homologs, and they would stand in mmseqs' null: dropping mmseqs from recruit moves mmseqs' cutoff in most families.

notes.author: jackroddy/21204bf1
notes.text: Shard 1 rescored the way reject does (tmp-claude/2026-10-06-mmseqs-rescore/): the reversals of all 112,038 recruits pooled, Pfam profile db against them with mmseqs -s 12 --max-seqs 1e9 -e 10 -k 6, 237 s at 48 threads. mmseqs scores 24% of the 102,661 nail-only recruits, 99% of both and of mmseqs-only. In the rescored per-family lists an mmseqs-only recruit is in mmseqs' top 5 for 3,635 of the 3,648 families that have one, rank 1 in 3,122, and holds half the top-5 slots. So the story holds after rescoring: nail's recruits do not displace them from mmseqs' null.

notes.author: jackroddy/21204bf1
notes.text: One-shard estimate of what dropping mmseqs from recruit does to mmseqs' cutoffs: against the committed data/mgy-cutoffs.tbl, whose null is ~10,600 decoys deep per family with mmseqs_5 at 34-42 bits, shard 1's recruits rescored by mmseqs put 358 decoys at or above mmseqs_5, 165 of them mmseqs-only (46%) and 193 nail-recruited. The tail decays 3.7x per bit, so keeping 54% of it lowers the top five by about 0.5 bits. Per-shard rank-1 counts were an artifact of a one-shard null. Not yet measured: the same for nail's cutoffs, which needs nail at reject settings over the pooled recruits.

notes.author: jackroddy/21204bf1
notes.text: Jack's verdict on the one-shard estimate: pointless. Which decoys built the committed mmseqs scores cannot be proven from recruits on one shard, only by the full run. What stands from shard 1: mmseqs-only recruits are about half of the recruits mmseqs scores at or above the committed mmseqs_5, and 0.4% of the top-10 mmseqs-only recruits over 100 shards are hmmer rejects. Open decision: recruit the 1000 shards with nail alone (39 h) or both (90 h).

notes.author: jackroddy/21204bf1
notes.text: nail at reject settings over shard 1's pooled 104,276 recruit reversals (tmp-claude/2026-10-06-nail-rescore/, 82 s at 48 threads): scores 82% of nail-only recruits, 95% of both, 26% of mmseqs-only (1,468 of 5,711). Against the committed nail cutoffs: 6 mmseqs-only recruits at or above nail_5, none above nail_1; nail-only 61, both 55. Of the scored mmseqs-only, nail rank 1 in 162 families, top 5 in 580. nail scores a pair 11-18 bits under mmseqs across every class; mmseqs-only pairs sit lowest, nail p50 12.3 vs mmseqs 30. 4,243 mmseqs-only recruits nail never scores; their mmseqs bits p50 31, same as the scored ones.
